hens_rule_text: Up to 12 poultry total per property (chickens, ducks, guinea fowl, pheasants, pigeons, quail, partridges and doves count together); no permit needed.
permit_notes: No permit or license required to keep poultry, but the facility must be maintained so it does not create noise or odor that disturbs neighbors.
setback_notes: The poultry facility (coop and run together) must be at least 25 ft from a residence on an adjacent property.
coop_rules: Coop (roofed shelter) capped at 120 sq ft; at least 3 sq ft of coop space and 6 sq ft of run space per bird. Geese, turkeys, emus, ostriches and similarly large birds are not allowed as backyard poultry.
zoning_notes: Rules found on the city's household animals page apply generally; not stated as varying by residential zoning district.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Salem, Poultry Keeping Rules (Household Animals and Pets)

research_notes: Facts come from a WebSearch extract of the city's own Poultry Keeping Rules page, which cites Salem Revised Code 50.710 by name; the live page returned a 403 to direct fetch, so the full page text was not independently read and slaughter was not addressed in the extract.
